decisions.reason: As a newly launched sensor module with its own product page, it fits the platform’s sensing logic and there is no clear evidence yet that its results fall below aspiration levels enough to justify redeploying resources.

Because the voltage measurement module is explicitly a 3.0 replacement for an earlier version, it likely serves established demand and represents normal iterative upgrading rather than a candidate for withdrawal.

The MQTT proxy extends the firm’s software and connectivity ecosystem, and under uncertainty a platform-oriented firm with relevant development capabilities would typically retain it while learning from market response.

The CAN bus interface module broadens communication options for industrial and embedded users, and with no sign of clear underperformance the firm would be inclined to keep this complementary module on the market.

The carbon dioxide sensor module has its own page and strengthens the environmental sensing range, so a boundedly rational management would usually continue it while assessing whether demand develops further.
The touch panel accessory supports usability and prototyping within the modular system, and absent evidence of a shortfall severe enough to trigger problemistic search it would likely be retained.
